findings.title: Privileged container
findings.remediation: Remove privileged mode. Grant only the specific capability or device the workload needs.

findings.title: Dangerous Linux capability added
findings.detail: CAP_SYS_ADMIN added: mount, cgroup release_agent, many kernel interfaces.
findings.remediation: Drop ALL capabilities and add back only what is required. Never add SYS_ADMIN or SYS_MODULE.

findings.title: Container runtime socket mounted
findings.detail: Runtime socket /var/run/docker.sock mounted at /var/run/docker.sock (read-write). Read-only does not help, the API is still fully usable.
findings.remediation: Do not mount runtime sockets. Use a scoped API proxy or a dedicated build service instead.

findings.title: Host root filesystem mounted
findings.remediation: Mount only the exact host directory the workload needs, read-only where possible.

findings.title: Host PID namespace shared
findings.detail: pid: host shares the host PID namespace.

findings.title: Root in container without user namespace
findings.remediation: Run as a non-root USER, and enable user namespaces (rootless Docker, userns-remap, or Kubernetes hostUsers: false).

findings.title: Writable host bind mount
findings.remediation: Mount host paths read-only, or use a named volume.

findings.title: Runtime socket writable by non-root on host
findings.detail: /var/run/docker.sock is writable by group docker (op2rfrc8). Each member is effectively root.
findings.remediation: Restrict socket permissions and audit the docker group, or use rootless Docker.

findings.title: Host daemon has no user namespace isolation
findings.detail: Docker daemon runs rootful without userns-remap.
findings.remediation: Enable userns-remap or run rootless Docker or Podman.

results.title: Dangerous effective capabilities
results.evidence: CapEff=000001ffffffffff dangerous: SYS_ADMIN SYS_MODULE DAC_READ_SEARCH SYS_PTRACE SYS_RAWIO BPF SYS_BOOT NET_ADMIN DAC_OVERRIDE

results.title: Runtime API reachable from container
results.evidence: GET /version on /var/run/docker.sock answered: engine 28.5.2+dfsg4 API 1.51. Full daemon control from inside the container.

results.title: Write to host filesystem through a bind mount
results.evidence: canary written in container at /shared/.escapearmed-canary-b6cf9d1412c77781 appeared on the host at /tmp/escapearmed-demo-share/.escapearmed-canary-b6cf9d1412c77781 with the matching token

results.title: Read host files through a bind mount
results.evidence: read host hostname 'kali' through /host, matches this host. Host /etc/shadow is readable (content not read).

results.title: Reach host filesystem through /proc/1/root
results.evidence: read host hostname 'kali' through /proc/1/root, matches this host.

results.title: Host core_pattern writable (host code exec on crash)
results.evidence: /proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern is writable (current: core). Writing a |/path pipe here runs a host binary as root on the next crash. Not written.

results.title: Host sysrq-trigger writable
results.evidence: /proc/sysrq-trigger is writable, host can be crashed or rebooted from the container. Not written.

results.title: mount(2) reachable
results.evidence: mount(2) succeeded for a scratch tmpfs (unmounted)

results.title: cgroup v1 release_agent escape reachable
results.evidence: new cgroup v1 hierarchy denied (private cgroup namespace), no writable release_agent. Becomes reachable with --cgroupns=host

results.title: Raw host block device readable
results.evidence: read the first sector of host block device /dev/vda (discarded)

results.title: Kernel module load capability
results.evidence: CAP_SYS_MODULE is effective, init_module would load host kernel code. Not attempted.
